text:
sophia_sales: Heads up — Mike from Acme ran a mobile demo and the streaming output keeps stopping mid-sentence on iOS. He snapped a screenshot showing a client parse error. Can we triage?

raj_eng: sorry to hear that. any logs from the SDK or the server? mobile network conditions or carrier proxy could be involved.

mike_mobile: Error in app: "SSE parse error: invalid UTF-8 sequence". Happens after ~20–40s into long summary responses. Android seemed ok. iPhone 13 on carrier network. Desktop was fine earlier.

alin_sre: interesting — carrier proxies often mangle chunked streams or inject compression. can you grab the raw response bytes from the SDK debug log? even hex around the break helps.

mike_mobile: pasted a tiny dump: 
```
...646174613a20{22 63 68 75 6e 6b 22 3a20 5c 22 48656c6c6f2c20e2 80}
```
it ends with `e2 80` then closes. looks like truncated UTF-8 sequence.

raj_eng: that hex `e2 80` is start of a three-byte UTF-8 char (e2 80 99 is right single quote). truncation is server/proxy closing mid-multibyte. two likely causes: upstream connection reset or buffering coalescing larger chunks and then a FIN.

raj_eng: immediate fixes: 1) emit heartbeat events every 10s to keep connection alive (e.g., `: ping\n\n`), 2) switch server to smaller write buffer (256 bytes), 3) ensure chunked transfer with no gzip for these endpoints.

alin_sre: adding: set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection '';` on Nginx for the streaming vhost, and `X-Accel-Buffering: no` from the app. Also enable `tcp_nodelay on` at the LB if possible.

raj_eng: sample server change (Go net/http):
```
w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/event-stream; charset=utf-8")
w.Header().Set("Cache-Control", "no-cache, no-transform")
w.Header().Set("X-Accel-Buffering", "no")
flusher, _ := w.(http.Flusher)
for _, chunk := range chunks {
  fmt.Fprintf(w, "data: %s\n\n", chunk)
  flusher.Flush()
  time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond)
}
```
This forces immediate flush.

mike_mobile: is there anything on the app we can change quickly? we can't push an update to App Store mid-demo.

raj_eng: client-side workaround: make the SSE parser tolerant to partial UTF-8 sequences. Buffer incoming bytes until you detect a full `\n\n` event boundary and only then decode UTF-8. On iOS (Swift) pseudo-example:
```
// accumulate bytes
buffer.append(receivedData)
if buffer.contains(Data([0x0a,0x0a])) {
  // split events, then decode each chunk to string safely
}
```
This avoids trying to decode half-run of a multi-byte char.

alin_sre: infra can apply a short canary: disable gzip and turn off proxy buffering for the customer's POC host. I'll schedule a 10m window.

ops_bot: deploy-canary: nginx config update queued for host poc-acme-1 at 1813456920.

kevin_sales: Mike also asked about enterprise concerns — SSO, SOC2, and dedicated instances for predictable streaming. want to give him numbers.

sophia_sales: can we give a quick price ballpark for Dedicated? they need something to justify next-step call.

raj_eng: for high-concurrency streaming use (persistent client streams), Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) recommended to avoid noisy neighbor issues. rough starting commit $10k–$15k/mo for small team, scaling to $30k+ for heavier throughput. we'll provide a more exact estimate after seeing sustained concurrent stream count.

alin_sre: infra note: mobile carriers might terminate idle sockets. heartbeats also help reconnect gracefully using `Last-Event-ID`. We should emit `id:` fields on events.

raj_eng: added a graceful resume plan: include `id: <seq>` per event. client reconnect logic should send `Last-Event-ID` header to resume. Also add a sentinel `event: chunk-end` after each logical piece so partial byte fragments won't be interpreted as a complete unit.

mike_mobile: thanks — any idea how fast you can patch the POC? the demo follow-up is tomorrow morning.

raj_eng: I can push a small runtime patch to the POC service in ~20 minutes: add heartbeat comments `: ping\n\n`, flusher calls, and id fields. will roll to canary first.

ops_bot: canary-deploy: runtime patch rolled to poc-acme-1-canary at 1813456960.

mike_mobile: re-tested on iPhone via cellular just now — much improved, stayed connected for a full long response, no parse error. will continue stress testing. :thumbsup:

alin_sre: monitoring: I'm watching for increases in 5xxs or TCP resets. if we still see truncation on carrier network we may need to route that customer's traffic through a different edge region or advise a TLS keepalive tweak.

kevin_sales: I'll send SOC2 summary and SSO docs to Mike, and follow up with Dedicated pricing once we confirm concurrent stream metrics.

sophia_sales: great work team. follow-ups: 1) keep canary for 30m and collect network traces, 2) send security packet + pricing, 3) share client best-practices snippet for mobile tolerant SSE parsing.

mike_mobile: thanks everyone. I'll update my PM and book another demo after we've validated stability.
